stories.title: Add Core Web Vitals optimization: hero image priority and lazy-loading
stories.description: The Hero component (Hero.tsx) likely uses a large banner image that is the Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) element. Without the `priority` prop on the Next.js Image component, the hero image is lazy-loaded, causing LCP scores above 4s on mobile — a Google ranking signal. Additionally, below-fold images should be explicitly lazy-loaded and sized with the `sizes` attribute to prevent Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS). Target: LCP < 2.5s, CLS < 0.1.
acceptanceCriteria: Hero image uses <Image priority> prop (no lazy loading on LCP element)
Hero image has explicit width, height, and sizes attribute set
All gallery images and below-fold images use loading='lazy' or default lazy behavior
No images use width/height that cause layout shift (CLS < 0.1)
PageSpeed Insights mobile score improves (document current score before, target 70+)
technicalNotes: Read site/src/components/Hero.tsx first to check current Image usage
Add priority prop to the hero <Image> component
Add sizes='(max-width: 768px) 100vw, 1920px' to hero image

Reference: https://nextjs.org/docs/pages/api-reference/components/image#priority
Test with: https://pagespeed.web.dev/ (mobile tab)
